title: Make tenant self-service user creation produce a login-capable user and leave no ghost membership on delete
goal: POST /system/user returns 200 and the new user shows up in the list with department and roles, but logging in returns 403 tenant.forbidden: CreateUser writes only system_user and never a tenant_memberships row, while GateSessionIssuance requires an active membership. The only workaround today is a platform administrator calling POST /system/tenant/:id/members for every user, which defeats the point of tenant self-service and is exactly the flow a customer hits first. Separately, deleting a user leaves its membership row active, so the member list accumulates __deleted_user_* entries that cannot be cleaned from the console. This wave closes both in the user service transaction.
findings: F1 (P0): CreateUser writes system_user only, so a tenant-created user has no tenant_memberships row and login is rejected by GateSessionIssuance with 403 tenant.forbidden.
F4 (P2): DeleteUser does not deactivate the membership, so tenant_memberships keeps an active row for a soft-deleted user and the member list shows __deleted_user_* ghosts.

out: Changing GateSessionIssuance or the login gate policy itself
Changing the default membership role away from member without a product decision

implementationNotes: Write the membership inside the same transaction that inserts system_user, so a failure cannot leave a user that cannot log in -- that half-state is the current defect.
Only create a membership when the resolved tenant is a real tenant (tenant_id != 0). Platform-scope users must keep working exactly as they do today.
Deactivation, not deletion, on user delete: the membership is an audit-relevant record of a past relationship, and GateSessionIssuance already treats non-active status as a denial.
Do not bypass BuiltinAdminUserID protections that BatchUpdateUserStatus already enforces.

runtimeEvidence: tenant-created user logs in on the first attempt with tenantId set, without any platform-side membership call
member list after deleting a user shows no __deleted_user_* row
platform-scope user creation still produces no membership and still logs in

humanGates: Confirm the default membership role for a tenant-created user is member (not inherit-from-creator).
Confirm whether a platform administrator creating a user inside a tenant also gets a membership (this packet says yes, because the user still needs to log in).
completionChecklist: CreateUser writes the membership in the same transaction for tenant-scope callers
New user logs in immediately; A3 acceptance passes
Ghost member rows no longer appear after delete
